To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ordinal mind-change complexity of identification from positive examples of the union of at most n pattern languages is Ωn, and this bound is tight.

(1) the ordinal mind change bound for identification of unions of pattern languages is ωk, where k is the number of variables used in the patterns, (2) this bound is essential, and (3) this result translates to learnability results for classes of logic programs and classes definable by elementary formal systems.

(i) The ordinal mind change complexity of identification in the limit of languages in the class formed by unions of n pattern languages is at least ωn; (ii) The ordinal mind changes complexity of identification in limit of languages in classes definable by elementary formal systems with length bound n is at least ω n; (iii) The ordinal mind complexity of learning logic programs with up to n predicates in the head is at least ω 2n.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the ordinal mind change complexty for identification from positive and negative data of classes of languages defined by various formalisms such as regular, pattern, and logic languages? What is the ordinal complexity for learning from positive data and for learning from positive and negative examples of classes of languages definable in various formalisms? What is the relationship between these two measures?
the ordinal mind change learning complexity of languages formed by the union of up to n context-free grammars.

the following questions: 1) What are the learnable classes of languages definable by length bounded elementary formal systems with n clauses? 2) What are the ordinal mind change complexities of the above classes of languages?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ordinal mind-change complexity of identification of classes of languages definable by length bounded elementary formal systems is ωn.
the learnability of a class is related to its ordinal mind change complexity and the latter is related to the number of clauses in the definition of the class.
the ordinal mind complexity for identification from text and identification from positive data are the same.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ordinal mind complexity of learning a class is ωn if the class can be characterized by a set of length bounded elementary formal systems with at most n clauses, where n is a constant.
the ordinal mind complexity of learning languages from positive data is essentially exponential.

we have established that the mind change complexity of identification from positive data for the classes of languages defined by unions of up n pattern languages, and by length-bounded EFS with up n clauses, are essentially the same.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ordinal mind complexity of a class of languages is determined by the number of clauses in a minimal length-bounded elementary system defining the class.
the ordinal mind-change complexity for learning classes of languages is a function of the size of the class of languages, and is not affected by the learning model.
the ordinal mind complexity of identification from positive data is not bounded by any computable ordinal.
